prompt:
An extract from the bay plan a ship's planner marks up before loading, the sheet the lashing gang works from.

The extract covers bay 03 and nothing else, drawn looking forward, so port is on the left of the sheet and starboard on the right. It is a grid of cells, five rows across and four tiers up, with each column of cells carrying its row number underneath it and each course of cells carrying its tier number beside it. The conventions on this trade are the ordinary ones: rows run outward from the centreline with 00 on the centreline itself, even numbers to starboard and odd numbers to port; deck tiers begin at 82 for the lowest tier on deck and go up in twos; and a box's position code is the two figures of the bay, then the two figures of the row, then the two figures of the tier, run together as six figures.

Today's stow list is three twenty foot boxes:
HLXU 1234567 -- one row to starboard of the centreline, second tier up on deck
MSCU 7654321 -- two rows to port of the centreline, lowest tier on deck
TGHU 2468101 -- on the centreline, top tier on deck

The gang works from this extract, so the cell each box occupies is shaded and carries that box's six figure code inside it, and every other cell of the grid is left empty. Which cell that is, and what the six figures come to, is the planner's work -- I am deliberately not telling you any row number, any tier number or any code. No working, no arrow and no note goes on the extract, and the codes and the margin numbers are large enough to read.

Answer yes or no only.
